jurisdictions.name: Indianapolis (Marion County)
jurisdictions.office: Department of Business and Neighborhood Services
notes: In-ground and above-ground pools, and hot tubs, need structural, improvement location and drainage permits, like any other structure.

An above-ground pool 30 inches or less deep and 15 feet or less across does not need a structural permit. One 18 inches or less deep and 15 feet or less in diameter does not need an improvement location permit.
A pool may not sit in a front yard, closer to a side lot line than the district's minimum side yard setback, or closer than five feet to a rear lot line.
The pool area must be enclosed by a safety pool cover meeting 675 IAC 20-4-27(c), or by a fence or other barrier with a self-closing, self-latching gate.

jurisdictions.name: Carmel
jurisdictions.office: Building and Code Services, Community Services Department
jurisdictions.portal_name: Online Permitting, with plan upload through Project Dox
notes: Carmel applicants file a residential permit online, then get an email to upload plans to the Project Dox submittal system once a permit number is assigned.
The city says residential projects must meet the 2020 Indiana Residential Code, which is the 2018 IRC with the 2020 Indiana amendments.
Carmel's pool inspection procedures list bonding and grounding and final inspections, with the equipotential bonding grid checked against NEC Section 680.26.
For pools without a cover, the same document requires a fence at least 5 feet high with self-closing, self-latching, lockable gates, under a separate fence permit.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Inspection Procedures - City of Carmel Building and Code Services

jurisdictions.name: Westfield
notes: Westfield lists a Residential Pool (RP) permit for in-ground pools, submitted through its Citizens Portal after registering an account.
Required documents include a site or plot plan showing property lines, existing structures, right-of-way and all easements, with scale, north arrow and address or lot number.
The pool page lists a State Construction Design Release (CDR) and an Erosion Control Application among the documents to prepare.
Construction documents must include a pool plan and a cross-section drawing of the pool, and review does not guarantee full compliance with the Indiana Building Code.

sources.title: Apply for a Permit - City of Westfield

jurisdictions.name: Lawrence (Marion County)
jurisdictions.office: City of Lawrence Department of Public Works
notes: Lawrence's Department of Public Works says every in-ground pool needs a permit, and above-ground pools need one if over 18 inches deep or over 15 feet across with an electrical connection.
The city handout says pool owners must also get an Improvement Location Permit from the Department of Business and Neighborhood Services in Marion County.
Pool permit applications must include a site plan showing the pool against structures, lot lines, easements and wetland buffers, plus the fence design with gate details.
The handout, based in part on the 2020 Indiana Residential Code, bars pools from front yards or within 5 feet of a rear lot line and says the structural design must be engineered.

sources.title: Swimming Pools and Hot Tubs - City of Lawrence Department of Public Works

jurisdictions.name: South Bend / St. Joseph County
jurisdictions.office: St. Joseph County / City of South Bend Building Department
jurisdictions.portal_name: City and County Swimming Pool Permit Application (online form)
notes: South Bend's Building Department lists a City and County Swimming Pool Permit Application among its residential permit forms, submitted through an online form.
The department's permits page says the 2020 Indiana Residential Code, based on the 2018 International Code, is in effect by state adoption.
Contractors must be registered or licensed with the Building Department. A residential owner-occupant may do their own work on their dwelling.

sources.title: Building Permits & Contractor Registrations - South Bend, Indiana

jurisdictions.name: Cicero (Hamilton County)
notes: Cicero and Jackson Township use a joint Plan Commission Swimming Pool/Spa Permit Application for residential and commercial pools, in-ground and above-ground.
The application says all pool and spa installations must follow Title 675 of the Indiana Administrative Code, 675 IAC 20-1 through 20-4.
The town asks for one copy of the pool construction plans, showing the required 5-foot wall, fence or barrier around the pool, and a site plan with property line dimensions and site improvements.
The form lists bonding, electrical and final inspections, and says detached fences, decks and accessory structures need their own permits.

sources.title: Cicero / Jackson Township Plan Commission Swimming Pool/Spa Permit Application

gaps: Only 2 jurisdictions verified. Indianapolis (indy.gov pages load only a script shell), Fort Wayne (Cloudflare/403), Fishers (Cloudflare), Evansville (403) and Bloomington (Cloudflare) could not be read.
Lafayette's residential projects page was opened but does not mention pools, so it was not used.
Carmel and Westfield: the code edition for pool barriers was not stated on the opened pages beyond the 2020 Indiana Residential Code (Carmel); Westfield does not name an edition.

Carmel's inspection document says the 5 ft fence rule, which is stricter than the state R326 4 ft figure on the existing JEBN page; the source was a city inspection procedure, so check with the city before relying on it.
